request.spec:
I work on several separate sheets of people. Let me type a name for the sheet I am working on
and show me which sheet is currently open. The people I add belong to the open sheet.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for this implementation's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
I work on several separate sheets of people. Let me type a name for the sheet I am working on
and show me which sheet is currently open. The people I add belong to the open sheet.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
You can now name the sheet you're working on, and the People page shows which sheet is open. `bin/e2e` passes: the acceptance test passes, and all 15 earlier test fixtures still seed and read back correctly.

**How it works on screen:** there's a "Sheet" box with an "Open sheet" button above the people list. After you open a sheet, its id is shown, the list shows only that sheet's people, and anyone you add goes onto it. A sheet is created the first time you add someone to it. Before you open a sheet, the page shows "none" and the people who don't belong to any named sheet, so existing data still appears.

**What changed:**
- **Database:** a new migration, `V6__sheets.sql`, adds a `sheet` table and gives each person a `sheet_id`. People without one are on the unnamed sheet.
- **Server:** listing and adding people take an optional `?sheet=` parameter. A person can now only choose patrons from their own sheet.
- **Test data:** the seed accepts a top-level `sheets` key, where each sheet has its own people and patrons. The read-back returns the same nested shape.
- **Front end:** the sheet box and the open sheet's id are on the People page, in `people.ts` and `people.service.ts`.

**Things to know:**
- **Person ids are shared across all sheets.** If a future fixture puts a person with the same id on two sheets, seeding will fail. Changing that would mean reworking how people and patrons are keyed.
- **The open sheet is forgotten on reload.** It isn't saved in the URL, so refreshing the page goes back to the unnamed sheet.
